html:
The First Intifada, Arabic for shaking off, was a mass Palestinian uprising against Israeli occupation in the West Bank and Gaza. It began in December 1987 in the Jabalia refugee camp in Gaza, after a traffic accident killed four Palestinians.

Young people threw stones at soldiers, and whole towns joined strikes, boycotts and refusals to pay taxes, run by local committees more than by the exiled PLO. Israel answered with mass arrests and force. Over a thousand Palestinians and about a hundred and sixty Israelis were killed.

The Islamist group Hamas was founded in Gaza at its start. The uprising put the occupation on world screens and led to the Madrid talks of 1991 and the Oslo Accords of 1993.
